## How the slice was produced

From a build of commit `a2482523` made with `tools/cts/mali-deqp-build.sh`:

```
BOARD_HOST=<board> tools/cts/mali-deqp-run.sh --build <build-dir> --out tools/cts/log/2026-11-21-t6-gles2-R373-a2482523 --rows 1-25 --tree build/r373/tree.txt --session adhoc
```

`BOARD_HOST` comes from the lease on `target:nanopc-t6`. The slice holds no host name, address, user name or serial; the raw dEQP logs stay out of git.

## Session R373 (plan #373 board-rerun)

- **origin/main commit:** `a2482523f609e5afcd7a554973bbde8d6558d103`. It holds all of plan #373's merged
  fixes: the integration tip `426ca097` is its ancestor. `deqp-gles2` (VK-GL-CTS `93bca018`) was built with
  `tools/cts/mali-deqp-build.sh --gles-lib`, and the library pair with `tools/mali/panthor-gles/build.sh`
  (release, `report-es2`). `check.sh` passed on the pair, and the build was within the GLIBC 2.41 /
  GLIBCXX 3.4.33 / CXXABI 1.3.15 floors.
- **Rows:** the 25 rows of `tools/cts/mali-gles2-tree.txt` that plan #373's fixes reach. They are copied
  unchanged (labels and filters) into `tree.txt`, the table the runner read; `meta.txt` names it by its
  build path `build/r373/tree.txt`. The rows are T6S1R03, R06, R11, R14 and R17; T6S2R01-R04, R06 and
  R13; T6S3R11-R22; and T6S4R01 and R08 (texturecubelod).
- **Command:** `tools/cts/mali-deqp-run.sh --build <build-dir> --out tools/cts/log/2026-11-21-t6-gles2-R373-a2482523 --rows 1-25 --tree build/r373/tree.txt
  --session adhoc --reruns <the four 2026-11-15 slices>`. It ran with `MALI_DEQP_MAIN_REF` naming this
  clone's copy of origin/main and `BOARD_HOST` from the lease. The runner accepts only S1..S4, smoke and
  adhoc as a session, so the session is `adhoc` and R373 is in the directory name. The runner exited 0.
- **`replaces=` was added to `meta.txt` by hand after the run.** It names the same four slices as
  `reruns=`. These rows were done in those slices, not Lost, so `reruns=` alone supersedes nothing, and a
  tally over the five slices then counts these 5944 cases twice. `replaces=` (the key of
  `mali-deqp-tally.py`) makes each R373 chunk stand in for the chunk with the same label. The runner does
  not write that key.
- **Boot id:** `b452f289-16e2-427e-9e32-64722b2fdedf` before and after (no reboot). `kmsg-session.txt`
  holds the `mali-kmsg.py` lines. There were 0 GPU faults, 0 job timeouts, 0 resets and 0 MMU faults. The
  50 kernel lines the run added are the runner's own start/end markers. The 3 `other_panthor` lines are
  probe lines from boot.
